statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 70% (high) as the OPEC+ November decision resolves as reported and the Riyadh refinery fire remains unconfirmed in supply terms.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it (00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October), where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk rather than on observed structure.
headline: OPEC+ core members are reported to hold November quotas steady, resolving the last unpriced weekend supply checkpoint and easing Stress a further notch while the CME halt keeps Tail at its floor
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed path was orderly two-way behaviour. The cash index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, in the lower part of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. Nasdaq-100 futures told the same story: a 31,282.50 high against a 31,061.75 settlement, roughly 0.7% off the high, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%, after a 15.30-16.24 range. A record high that is fully retraced into the close is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that Tail measures.

Stress is marked down a further notch to 70% from the 73% published an hour earlier, and is now 9 points below the 79% ceiling reached at 09:00Z. The reason is specific rather than drift: the last unpriced weekend supply checkpoint has resolved. The seven core OPEC+ members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, met at 11:00 GMT on 4 October and are reported to have agreed in principle to hold November output targets steady. Reporting around that meeting notes the group pumped 25 million barrels a day in August, roughly 5 million below pre-war February levels, with Gulf exports running at 60-80% of normal and further target changes unlikely before 2027. WTI was quoted near 91.26 dollars, down 1.73%, with Brent at 102.72, up 0.46%.

The Saudi escalation channel remains unresolved but still unquantified. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said strikes on an Aramco facility in Riyadh on 3 October were precise and direct and caused fires; satellite thermal detections and open-source imagery are consistent with a significant fire and probable emergency flaring. A Saudi-led coalition spokesman, Turki al-Maliki, called the Houthi account misleading, and neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed the cause, any damage, any outage period, or any impact on production, refining or exports. Scale matters here: the Riyadh refinery is a domestic facility of roughly 126,000 barrels a day rather than export infrastructure. The March strikes on Ras Tanura, a refinery of more than 500,000 barrels a day, did force a temporary shutdown with a restart on 13 March and did move oil prices, which is the precedent that would matter if an outage were confirmed; earlier Houthi attempts on Yanbu in late September were intercepted with no reported damage.

What keeps Stress firmly in the high band is structural rather than new. The Strait of Hormuz has been largely closed to commercial shipping since 28 February, Brent remains above 100 dollars, and the Federal Reserve H.15 released 2 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 5-year at 5.01%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%, against a 3.88% federal funds effective rate. The Iran channel is genuinely two-sided, which argues against reading it as a one-way Tail driver: the diplomatic track has stalled since the Iranian delegation was told to leave the United States on 1 October after talks over a seven-day Hormuz roadmap failed to close, and further escalation has been described only as possible without any timeline, while mediated contact continues.

The macro mix behind Friday's record close is stagflationary rather than directional. September payrolls rose only 29,000 against expectations above 80,000, unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000, which left October Fed hike odds priced well below even, in the high teens to low twenties across reported measures, although a December hike remains priced and the Fed raised rates at its September meeting. The week ahead is light: ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October is expected close to its prior mid-50s reading, the FOMC minutes from the September meeting at 18:00Z on 7 October are the main scheduled risk and the kind of multi-stage repricing event that warrants care, jobless claims follow on 8 October, and preliminary Michigan sentiment near 48 with one-year inflation expectations near 4.6% closes the week on 9 October. With Q3 earnings not starting in volume until mid-October, oil and the long end of the Treasury curve are the likely primary drivers.

The forecast therefore holds Tail between 3% and 6% through the closed Sunday hours, steps it to 10% in the final hour before the reopen, and raises it to 21% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it. That elevation is gap and discontinuity risk conditional on an unknown first print, not observed structure, and a contained reopen trading both sides of the 31,061.75 futures settlement would retire it quickly. The published decay afterwards assumes orderly two-way discovery; a gap that holds without meaningful retracement, a second leg after a failed retracement, or a confirmed Saudi export outage would each invalidate that assumption. The shared deterministic Finviz context file was stale by several days, collected 29 September and only partially complete, so it contributed no current evidence and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary and reputable current sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 4% in the first slot and 3% in every hour after it, while Stress bottomed at 52% at 14:00Z on 3 October and then ratcheted steadily to a 79% ceiling by 09:00Z on 4 October before easing to 73% at 10:00Z as the weekend's open checkpoints began to resolve. Confidence stayed in the 83-87% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held between 3% and 6% through 20:00Z while Stress is marked down to 70% as the OPEC+ November decision resolves as reported. Tail then steps to 10% in the final closed hour and is raised to 21% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which together form the published danger window. It decays conditionally to 8% by 10:00Z on 5 October on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that a gap holding without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 78% at the reopen and recovers to 85% once a continuous path is observable again.
